texts.value: Sperm-specific catalytic alpha subunit of the Na(+)/K(+)-ATPase responsible for ATP-dependent Na(+)/K(+) exchange across the plasma membrane. Transports 3 Na(+) ions out of the cell and 2 K(+) ions into the cell for each ATP hydrolyze (PubMed:16861705). Plays an essential for sperm motility, capacitation, and male fertility by maintaining ionic gradients required for flagellar function and signaling (By similarity)

reaction.name: 2 K(+)(out) + 3 Na(+)(in) + ATP + H2O = 2 K(+)(in) + 3 Na(+)(out) + ADP + phosphate + H(+)

texts.value: Specifically inhibited by an endogenous cardiac glycoside, ouabain

The sodium/potassium-transporting ATPase is composed of a catalytic alpha subunit, an auxiliary non-catalytic beta subunit and an additional regulatory subunit, called FXYD. There are four, three and seven isoforms for the alpha, beta and regulatory subunits, respectively, among which the expression of the alpha isoforms is tissue-specific (PubMed:16861705). The particular alpha/beta/FXYD combination in each tissue defines the pump's kinetic and regulatory properties. Interacts with ATP1B1 (PubMed:16861705, PubMed:39596464). Interacts with ATP1B3 (PubMed:16861705)
In mature sperm, located in the principle piece of the sperm flagellum
Specifically expressed in testis (PubMed:16175638, PubMed:16861705). Found in very low levels in skeletal muscle. Expressed in mature sperm (at protein level) (PubMed:16175638)

Undergoes ATP-driven conformational changes associated with a transient phosphorylation that shifts the pump conformation from inward-facing (E1) to outward-facing state (E2). In the inward-facing state (E1), it binds three Na(+) ions from the cytoplasm and becomes phosphorylated at the active site Asp, triggering a structural shift. In the outward-facing state (E2), Na(+) is released outside the cell, two K(+) ions bind, and dephosphorylation of the active site Asp restores the inward-facing conformation, allowing K(+) release into the cytoplasm and completion of the cycle
Belongs to the cation transport ATPase (P-type) (TC 3.A.3) family. Type IIC subfamily
